What is Verilog and what is it used for?

Verilog is a Hardware Description Language (HDL) used to model and simulate digital circuits. It is an IEEE standard (1364) widely used for FPGA and ASIC design at the register-transfer level (RTL).

Key tools:
- **Icarus Verilog (iverilog)** — free open-source simulator
- **Verilator** — fast simulation
- **Xilinx Vivado / Intel Quartus** — FPGA synthesis
- **GTKWave** — waveform viewer

```verilog
// hello.v — simulation only
module hello;
    initial begin
        $display("Hello, World!");
        $display("Hello, %s!", "Verilog");
        $finish;
    end
endmodule
```

```bash
iverilog -o hello hello.v && ./hello
# Hello, World!
# Hello, Verilog!
```

SystemVerilog (IEEE 1800) extends Verilog with OOP for verification.
